nodes.label: Finding
nodes.text: P1 shipment resolution for disputed TXN-C19-01: TXN-C19-01 is linked to PO ORD-C19-01 by FOR_ORDER E-0508184; the PO is linked to shipment SHP-C19-01 by SHIPPED_AS E-0508185. SHP-C19-01 records carrier QuickShip, tracking QS-C19-0001 and ship date 2026-09-05. DELIVERED_TO E-0508186 links it to ADR-C19-DEPOT, with postcode 07102, street 4 Foundry Access Road, unit Dock 9, Newark; POD reference is 'warehouse scan' and signer is 'dock clerk'. The graph therefore supports a delivered-to relationship, but has no explicit delivery-status field or delivery-event timestamp beyond the shipment's ship date.

nodes.text: The carrier record for SHP-C12B identifies a door photo, but records delivery to 601 Grove Lane, unit 3C, Queens, NY 11372, while the customer's recorded address is 610 Grove Lane, unit 3C, Queens, NY 11372. The street number differs; no signer is recorded. This directly supports a delivery-address mismatch, although the underlying photo and delivery timestamp are not available in the graph.

nodes.text: P2 address comparison: the disputed order's delivered destination is ADR-C19-DEPOT (4 Foundry Access Road, Dock 9, Newark, NJ 07102) via DELIVERED_TO E-0508186. The cardholder CUS-C19-01 lived at ADR-C19-HOME-01 (201 Orchard Street, Unit 1A, Brooklyn, NY 11211) under LIVES_AT E-0508181, valid from 2022-01-01 with no end date; this interval covers the order timestamp 2026-09-03T11:00:00Z. The delivery destination differs from the valid-at-order residence in street, unit, city and postcode, so the delivery record does not establish delivery to the customer's home. The same depot is used by the eight C19 orders: SHP-C19-01 through SHP-C19-08 each resolve through their respective SHIPPED_AS and DELIVERED_TO edges to ADR-C19-DEPOT.

nodes.text: P3 missing-link assessment: no graph edge or PurchaseOrder property supplies an order shipping address for ORD-C19-01, so the merchant's original requested destination cannot be compared directly with the delivered destination. No explicit delivery-status property, delivery timestamp, geolocation, or separate proof-of-delivery document/reference node is present; only DELIVERED_TO E-0508186's POD text 'warehouse scan' and signer 'dock clerk' are available. The dispute DSP-2026-90019 also has no linked HAS_EVIDENCE or REQUESTED/EvidenceRequest record in the traversed graph. These omissions limit the record to a delivery-address assertion, not verified receipt by the customer.

nodes.evidence_path: CUS-C12-01..04-[HAS_PHONE]->PHN-C12-SHARED; CUS-C12-01..04-[LIVES_AT]->ADR-C12-RING; TXN-C12-01..04-[FROM_DEVICE E-0508090]->DEV-C12-SHARED; TXN-C12-01..04 delivered to ADR-C12-RING; CUS-C12B phone PHN-C12-SHARED valid_to=2025-12-31; CUS-C12B-[LIVES_AT]->ADR-C12B-HOME; TXN-C12B has no FROM_DEVICE/FROM_IP; SHP-C12B delivered to ADR-C12B-WRONG
nodes.text: A delivery-ring pattern exists among four other 2026 claims: CUS-C12-01 through CUS-C12-04 share PHN-C12-SHARED and live at ADR-C12-RING (29 Lantern Court, unit 1), with four Harborlane Market transactions delivered to that same address and a shared device DEV-C12-SHARED. Ari Bell's case is not temporally or identifier-linked to that ring: Ari's phone edge ended 2025-12-31, Ari lives at ADR-C12B-HOME (610 Grove Lane, unit 3C), and TXN-C12B has no FROM_DEVICE or FROM_IP edge; the disputed parcel was delivered to a different address ADR-C12B-WRONG (601 Grove Lane, unit 3C). This supports a separate ring elsewhere, not attribution of TXN-C12B to it, and provides no affirmative ATO signal for Ari.

nodes.evidence_path: DSP-2026-90122-[REQUESTED E-0508151]->ERQ-C12B (merchant, 2026-10-19, no_response, deadline_passed=true); ORD-C12B; SHP-C12B-[DELIVERED_TO]->ADR-C12B-WRONG; PRC-004; VISA-13.1@2026-04-18; LFB-SOP-DSP-001@v7
nodes.text: Merchant evidence was expressly requested for DSP-2026-90122 and was unanswered: ERQ-C12B is a merchant request with deadline 2026-10-19, deadline_passed=true, responded_at null, status no_response. Under PRC-004 and the missing-evidence rule, delivery proof unavailable because of that unanswered request is resolved cardholder-favourably for the not-received issue; this is an adverse-evidence/default treatment of the missing proof, not a finding that silence alone proves every element. The available records independently show the order was for two lamps and the delivery was to ADR-C12B-WRONG with a door photo and no signer, while Ari's home is ADR-C12B-HOME.

nodes.label: Finding
nodes.evidence_path: CRD-C12B-[ISSUED_ON]->ACC-C12B (kind=credit, credit_limit=7500); LFB-SOP-DSP-001@v7; REGZ-1026.13; VISA-13.1@2026-04-18; REGE-1005.11; LFB-SOP-DSP-006@v4; ERQ-C12B
nodes.text: The account is a credit account (ACC-C12B, credit_limit 7500), so SOP-DSP-001 routes this case to Regulation Z, not Regulation E. Accordingly, the Regulation E provisional-credit rule in REGE-1005.11 / LFB-SOP-DSP-006 is not the applicable basis for this case; the applicable resolution is the Visa 13.1 not-received condition and Reg Z billing-error framework (REGZ-1026.13), with the merchant's unanswered delivery-proof request handled under PRC-004. The 2026-10-19 miss alone is not being used as a rule; the request record and the wrong-address/no-signer delivery records are cited.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Merchant MER-C19 (Yesterday Goods) should not be treated as having a generally reliable delivery pattern for the observed period: newer graph evidence shows eight September 2026 shipments routed to one Newark depot rather than the cardholders' recorded homes. Treat the earlier reliability note as stale and require transaction-level delivery verification.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Reusable missing-evidence rule: when a merchant is actually asked for delivery proof and the request passes with no response, the unavailable requested proof is not presumed to favor the merchant. Apply that adverse-evidence treatment only to the requested proof and combine it with independently observed delivery facts; do not treat silence alone as proof of every element.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Reusable delivery-evidence pattern: a carrier DELIVERED_TO record does not by itself establish receipt when the recorded destination differs from the customer's address valid at the transaction time. Repeated delivery to a depot or other non-home location, a missing/limited signer or POD record, and absent delivery metadata warrant treating receipt as unestablished until the original order ship-to and complete carrier proof are verified; do not infer what an unavailable image would show.

nodes.label: MemoryNote
nodes.text: Reusable anti-decoy rule: a shared-identifier delivery cohort should remain separate from a target dispute unless a temporally valid identifier and transaction linkage connect them. A different merchant, address or device cohort, especially where the target has no FROM_DEVICE/FROM_IP linkage, is not sufficient to infer account takeover or coordinated fraud.
